name: takeoff: brief read
belief: This is a document-QA build. The grading signal is listening, not technical flash: the brief says a modest build that proves you listened beats an impressive one that ignores the client.

name: prior: the test is the amendment
belief: Doug's trust test is the demo's spine: ingest Amendment 1 and show the deadline moving Nov 13 -> Dec 4 and the deposit moving $75,000 -> $100,000, with section citations for both the base text and the superseding text.
evidence: Transcript p.5 (Doug: 'Show me it noticing the amendment'); Amendment A1.1, A1.2

name: prior: the sample questions are traps
belief: Several sample questions are planted tests: Q1/Q2 are stale unless the amendment is applied; Q5 (union labor) must return 'not addressed in the RFP'; Q7 (call our ISO contact) must cite 4.2 prohibited contact; Q12 (revise cap upward) must cite 7.4 'may not be revised upward'; Q3 must note A1.4 confirms the weights are unchanged.
evidence: sample_questions.txt vs RFP 4.2, 7.4, A1.4; Nina's two non-negotiables p.4

name: prior: constraints are the architecture
belief: Indexing and retrieval run locally (Sam); only the minimal cited excerpts plus the question leave the box, and each model call's payload is logged; ingestion is idempotent by content hash (Doug: no duplicate trackers); no portal scraping, no DMS integration, no drafting of bid language (out of scope).

name: open unknowns
belief: Unresolved: the live-question path (monday board item -> webhook vs poller), GraphQL API vs monday MCP for writes, whether retrieval needs embeddings at all for a ~118-page doc vs section-structured lookup, and what the briefing video adds beyond the PDF.
evidence: Brief p.7 (live question during demo); briefing video not yet transcribed
